checklist.evidence: Sync: webhook or nightly incremental re-index. Deletions must propagate, or the bot will cite retired articles.
split by heading structure, about 300–600 tokens, with the title and breadcrumb prepended to each chunk.
150–300 real questions from past tickets and search logs. Each has a reference answer and the correct source articles.
if the top rerank score is below a threshold, don't answer. Offer handoff or suggest related articles.
create a ticket with the conversation transcript, retrieved articles, and the bot's attempted answer
Resist prompt injection, since docs and user input are untrusted.
tenant isolation if there is private content
Actions (later): authenticated tools such as order status, each with explicit permissions and confirmation.
report unanswered questions and low-confidence topics to the docs team as a gap list.
cache frequent questions, use a smaller model for query rewriting, and cap context size.

traps.evidence: Say "I don't know" when the context is insufficient.
tenant isolation if there is private content
run the suite in CI on any change to the prompt, chunking, embedding model, or LLM.
BM25 plus dense embeddings, merged with reciprocal rank fusion.

note: Solid, competent generic RAG support-bot plan with good eval and grounding, but thin on access control, privacy specifics, cost numbers, ops/rollback and explicit assumptions.
